/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 11 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3507 (-14)
Baltic Capesize Index: 6080 (-42)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2407 (-2)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1719 (6)
Baltic Handysize Index: 940 (9)
CAPESIZE
The market ended the week on a quieter note, with activity slowing across both basins as the BCI 182 5TC eased by $380 to $55,139. In the Pacific, trading was subdued, with only one miner active in the market, resulting in limited fixture activity. The C5 index was essentially unchanged, slipping just $0.040 to $17.845. The sole miner entered the market bidding around $17.40 against offers in the low-$18s before ultimately fixing at $17.75, matching yesterday's level. With little additional demand emerging, the basin ended the week on a flat note. The Atlantic also wrapped up the week more quietly, with limited engagement around index dates and increasing talk of early vessels beginning to build up. While prompt activity remained scarce, there was market discussion of $42.50 being achieved for slightly forward positions, although this remained unconfirmed. The C3 index edged higher by $0.396 to $42.123, providing the day's only notable positive movement.
PANAMAX
Market sources today highlighted the continued tightness of prompt tonnage in both the Western Mediterranean and West Africa, although vessel availability in the North Continent is still reported to be relatively ample. Several Owners have indicated a preference for Atlantic trading, with some market participants suggesting this may be in anticipation of the upcoming US Gulf grain season. As a result, the P1A route closed unchanged from yesterday, while the P2A index recorded a modest increase. Market participants also noted that activity in the Pacific has eased compared with previous sessions. However, prompt tonnage availability in South China is reported to be tightening. The P5TC index declined by $22 today, bringing the week to a close at $21,662.

Atlantic
The Arktos (82,179 2012) was said to have been placed on subjects basis sailing Gangavaram 29 August for an EC South America fronthaul at around $23,500-$24,000. The scrubber fitted Marathon (82028 2026) open Da Nang 10 September was said to have fixed an EC South America to SE Asia to ADM at $26,000, with the scrubber benefit for Charterers.

Asia
The Radiant (87,334 2010) open Bahodopi 15 September fixed to Pan Ocean for an Indonesia to South Korea, although the rate was unknown. The Geopride (81,902 2013) open Longkou 15/16 September fixed for North Pacific round trip to Cargill at $21,250 with others suggesting the rate to be $20,500. Guaransea was said to have placed on subjects the MSXT Echo (85,187 2021) open Kwangyang 15 September for an EC Australia coal stem to China at $24,350.
SUPRAMAX
A slow afternoon slide into the weekend, as the 11TC average gained $551 over the week to finish at $21,728. There was again a flurry of reported trades from the US Gulf, whilst elsewhere remained fairly flat, as most decided to leave things until next week.

Atlantic
The Jin Hong (61,414 2011) fixed on voyage basis with ArcelorMittal 55,000/10 iron ore Buchanan to Qingdao at $39.40 fio for 22-26 September dates and LDC were linked to a Supra/Ultra from West Africa to India with manganese ore at 20,500 with redelivery Singapore, having been linked with the BH Tangshan (64,622 2026) open Lagos 13 September redelivery East coast India earlier in the week. The New Dedication (63,434 2018) was heard to be on subjects with Oldendorff for a petcoke stem US Gulf to India at $38,000, whilst the Pan Regina (63,243 2020) went to Norden delivery Tarragona 9 September via Puerto Drummond to the East option India at $23,000, again with petcoke. The Xin An Ning (55,256 2009) Brownsville 20 September went on subjects delivery SW Pass for a trip via Panama with grains to Singapore-Japan at $30,000 to MOL and XO fixed the Maro Maro (61,134 2022) delivery Puerto Drummond for a trip Continent-Baltic (intention Poland) with coal at $30,000. The Jay (57,809 2010) New Orleans 12 September was placed on subjects basis delivery Mobile for a trip UK-Contintent with woodpellets at $28,250 with Norden, although another source advised the rate to be $27,000.

Asia
HMM booked the Star Apus (63 2014) Mundra 15-17 September for a trip via Kandla intention salt to the Far East at around $17,000, basis scrubber benefit for Owners.
HANDYSIZE
The week ended on a firm note, with sentiment generally healthy across both the Atlantic and Asian markets. The BHSI closed at 940, while the 7TC average increased by $174 to finish at $16,925. The US Gulf was very active, with improved levels continuing to be seen and fixtures concluded well above last-done levels. The Vera London (33,471 2013) was fixed from New York to Iskenderun with scrap at around $16,500–$16,750, while the Fanoula (41,240 2025) was placed on subjects from SW Pass to the West Mediterranean with grains at $20,000. The Continent and Mediterranean saw some fresh demand, with a 37,000-dwt vessel open Black Sea on 15 September reported fixed for a fronthaul trip via COGH at $15,500, although further details were not disclosed. The South Atlantic maintained steady dynamics, with the Lake St. Claire (27,781 2005) open South Brazil reported fixed with sugar, although further details were not disclosed. In the Pacific, market fundamentals showed little change, with rates generally holding steady around last-done levels.

Market Fundamentals
South Korea Curbs Coal Generation

On 10 September, South Korea’s Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE) announced plans to minimise coal-fired power generation from 19 September to 15 November, McCloskey reports. The initiative comes as autumn shoulder season is expected to bring milder weather and lower humidity. However, the extent of the curbs will be determined by power demand and renewable power generation during the period. South Korea’s thermal coal imports stood 1.4 Mt higher than the year prior, at 10.1 Mt in July, McCloskey data show.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape was mixed today, with early weakness followed by some afternoon recovery. September was under a lot of pressure today with 51,500 trading early, down to around 51,100–51,250, where it remained through the afternoon. October opened around 48,500–48,800 before falling to 47,800–48,000 late morning, then recovered to 48,500–48,600 in the afternoon. November eased from 45,650 to around 45,150–45,500, while December moved from 43,250 to 43,000. Q4 fell from around 46,000 to 45,400 before recovering to 45,750 later in the session. WHILE SENTIMENT REMAINS POSITIVE, THE WIDE GAP BETWEEN BIDS AND OFFERS HAS RESULTED IN A MORE MEASURED TRADING ENVIRONMENT. HIGHER BUNKER PRICES AND A SOFTER PAPER MARKET TOWARDS THE END OF THE WEEK ALSO TEMPERED SOME OF THE EARLY MOMENTUM. NOPAC ENJOYED A STRONG START TO THE WEEK WITH HEALTHY GRAIN DEMAND FOR LATE SEP-EARLY OCT SUPPORTING FIXING LEVELS AT $21,750 BKI CJK. AS THE WEEK PROGRESSED AND PROMPT STEMS WERE FIXED, CHARTERERS SHOWED LESS URGENCY TO COVER AND MOMENTUM SLOWED. HOWEVER, LEVELS WERE STILL STRONG WITH SPREADS AT $22.5K VS $23.5K BKI CJK. THE NORTH REMAINS WELL SUPPORTED WITH HEALTHY DEMAND FOR EARLY-MID OCT. E.AUS WAS THE DRIVER OF THE PACIFIC MARKET THROUGH THE FIRST HALF OF THE WEEK, WITH STRONG MINERAL DEMAND PUSHING FIXING LEVELS INTO THE LOW TO MID-$22K'S BKI CJK. HEALTHY DEMAND FOR LATE SEP-EARLY OCT DATES HELPED ABSORB AVAILABLE TONNAGE AND KEEP OWNERS FIRMLY IN CONTROL OF NEGOTIATIONS. HOWEVER, DEMAND EASED TOWARDS THE END OF THE WEEK AS MANY SEPCARGOES WERE COVERED, LEAVING OCTOBER BUSINESS AS THE PRIMARY FOCUS. SPREADS FOR EAUS RV WERE AROUND $22.7K VS 24K BKI CJK. INDO REMAINED SUPPORTED THROUGHOUT THE WEEK BUT FAILED TO MATCH THE STRENGTH SEEN IN NOPAC AND E.AUS. HOWEVER, STRONG DEMAND FOR MINERALS EX S.CHINA AND INDO INTO INDIA PROVIDED A VALUABLE ALTERNATIVE OUTLET FOR TONNAGE, WITH REPORTED BUSINESS PAYING LOW-MID $21K'S BKI HK. COMPETITION FROM A STRONG ECSA FH MARKET AND E.AUS DEMAND ALSO HELPED SUPPORT MODERN KAMSARMAXES IN S.CHINA AND SE ASIA. BY WEEK'S END, STANDARD INDO RV LEVELS WERE AROUND $20,250 BKI HK, ALTHOUGH SOME OWNERS APPEARED MORE WILLING TO COMPROMISE AS DEMAND THINNED. LOOKING AHEAD, THE PACIFIC MARKET REMAINS FUNDAMENTALLY WELL SUPPORTED WITH CARGO VOLUMES STILL HEALTHY ACROSS THE BASIN. WHILE CHARTERERS HAVE SHOWN SOME RESISTANCE TO HIGHER LEVELS TOWARDS THE END OF THE WEEK, THE OVERALL SUPPLY-DEMAND BALANCE REMAINS FAVOURABLE.
